 Aged about 21 years,
 No.07, Karadihalli Village,
 Banavara, Hassan - 573 112.
 (Sri K. T. Madhu, Advocate)
 Vs.
Respondents: 1. Shivaraj T. E. S/o Eswarappa,
 R/o Talalur Village & Post,
 Hassan District.
 (RC Owner of Maruti LMV Car  bearing No.KA-13-N-5358)
 (Sri K. V. Pradeepa, Advocate)
 2 MVC No.1749/2022  2. United India Insurance Co. Ltd.,

 (Sri B. R. Basavaraju, Advocate)
 JUDGMENT

This is petition filed under Section 163-A of Motor Vehicles Act, seeking compensation of Rs.10,00,000/- from the respondents, on account of grievous injuries sustained by the petitioner in a road traffic accident.

2. The brief facts of the case are as follows:
On 13-11-2021 at about 8.30 p.m., the petitioner was a pillion rider on the motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-13-EM- 2481, ridden by Dhananjaya S/o Jagadeesh in a moderate speed, by observing all the traffic rules and regulations.

When they reached B.H. road, Bommenahalli Gate, Kasaba Hobli, Tiptur Taluk, Tumakuru, at that juncture the driver of the car bearing Reg. No.KA-13-N-5358, coming from opposite direction, drove the same in a rash and negligent manner, without observing the traffic rules and regulations and dashed against the motorcycle of the petitioner.
Due to the said impact, the petitioner and rider of the said motorcycle fell down and sustained grievous injuries.
Immediately after the accident, the petitioner was shifted to Government Hospital, Tiptur, wherein she took treatment as an in-patient.
Earlier to the accident, she was student, studying in II PUC.

But, due to the accidental injuries, she is unable to attend the extra-curricular activities during her educational career and she has become permanently disabled and thereby lost her learning capacity.
The Tiptur Rural Police have registered the case against the driver of the said car, for the offences punishable under Section 279, 337 and 304(A) of IPC.
The respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle.
Hence, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Therefore, it is prayed to allow the petition and award compensation of Rs.10,00,000/- with interest.
3. On service of notice to the respondents, the respondents No.1 and 2 have appeared through their counsel.
The respondent No.2 has filed its written statement.
Whereas, the respondent No.1 did not choose to file his written statement.
4. The respondent No.2 in its written statement has denied all the allegations made in the petition.
It has admitted the issuance of insurance policy in respect of car bearing No.KA-13-N-5358 and its validity as on the date of accident.
It seeks protection under Sections 147 and 149(2) of Motor Vehicles Act.
Further, it has sought for permission to contest even on behalf of respondent No.1 under Section 170 of the Motor Vehicles Act.

It has contended that, the petition is liable to be dismissed for non-joinder of necessary party i.e. owner and insurer of the motorcycle bearing Reg.

2 No.KA-13-EM-2481.
Further it is contended that, the driver of the insured car was not holding valid and effective driving licence to drive the said vehicle, as on the date of accident.
It has denied the age, avocation and income of the petitioner.

It has contended that, at the time of alleged accident,
the petitioner was not at all wearing the prescribed ISI marked helmet and hence sustained injuries to her head and she was solely responsible for her personal injuries by violating the mandatory provisions of law under the Motor Vehicle Act and rules.
Further it is contended that, the rider of the motorcycle himself was negligent in causing the accident, as such the petition was not maintainable for one's own negligence.
The petitioner in colluding with the police has filed a false complaint in order to wangle an award.
Hence, this respondent is not liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner and the petition is liable to be dismissed against this respondent.
It has denied the occurrence, mode of the accident and also involvement of the car as mentioned in the claim petition.
Further it is contended that, the compensation claimed is highly excessive and exorbitant.
For the above denials and contentions, it prayed for dismissal of the petition.
5. On the basis of rival pleadings of both the sides, the following issues are framed:
ISSUES

1 . Whether the petitioner proves that, she has sustained grievous injuries in the road traffic accident, arose out of the usage of Car bearing Reg. No.KA-13-N- 5358 on the public road, alleged to have occurred on 13-11-2021 at about 8.30 p.m., on B.H. road,
Bommanahalli Gate, Kasaba Hobli, Tiptur Taluk, Tumakuru ?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?

If so, what is the quantum and from whom ?
3.
What order or Award ?
6. In order to prove her case, the petitioner has got examined herself as P.W.1 and got marked 7 documents as Ex.P.1 to 7.
On the other hand, the respondents No.1 and 2 have not adduced any evidence on their behalf.
7. I have heard the arguments of both the sides and perused the entire material placed on record.

In support of his arguments, the learned counsel for petitioner has relied on the following decisions:
i. Syed Yaseen V/s Nasreen Banu and others, in MFA No.5130/2015 (MV-I),
Judgment dated 30-06-2025.
ii. New India Assurance Co. Ltd., V/s Urmila Halder, reported in 2025 ACJ 244.
iii.

8. My findings on the above issues are as under:

3 Issue No.1: Affirmative Issue No.2: Partly Affirmative Issue No.3: As per the final order, for the following:
REASONS 9. Issue No.1: It is specific case of the petitioner that, on 13-11-2021 at about 8.30 p.m., when he was pillion rider on the motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-13-EM-2481, ridden by one Dhananjaya S/o Jagadeesh, on B.H. road, Bommenahalli Gate, Kasaba Hobli, Tiptur Taluk, Tumakuru, at that time the driver of car bearing Reg. No.KA-13-N-5358, coming from opposite direction, drove the same in a rash and negligent manner, without observing any of the traffic rules and regulations and dashed against the motorcycle of the petitioner.
Due to the said impact, the petitioner and rider of the said motorcycle fell down and sustained grievous injuries.
Further it is contended that, earlier to the accident, she was student, studying in II PUC.

But, due to the accidental injuries, she is unable to attend the extra- curricular activities during her educational career and she has become permanently disabled and thereby lost her learning capacity.
10. In order to prove her case, the petitioner has examined herself as P.W.1 by filing examination-in-chief affidavit, wherein she has reiterated entire averments made in the petition.
Further, in support of her oral evidence, the petitioner has got marked total 7 documents as Ex.P.1 to 7.

Out of the said documents, Ex.P.1 is true copy of F.I.R., Ex.P.2 is true copy of first information statement, Ex.P.3 is certified copy of spot mahazar, Ex.P.4 is certified copy of Motor Vehicles Accident report, Ex.P.5 is true copy of wound certificate, Ex.P.6 is certified copy of charge-sheet and Ex.P.7 is notarized copy of Aadhar card.

11. On meticulously going through the above police documents marked as Ex.P.1 to 6, prima-facia it reveals that, the accident in question has taken place due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-13-EM-2481 and dashing the same to the oncoming car bearing No.KA-13-N-5358.
Due to said impact, the petitioner has fell down on the road and sustained grievous injuries all over the body.

The investigation officer in his final report, marked as Ex.P.6, has clearly stated that, the said accident is caused due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-13-EM-2481.
12.

At the outset it is pertinent to note that, in the present case, the date, time and place of accident,
involvement of car bearing Reg. No.KA-13-N-5358 in the said accident, issuance of insurance policy by the respondent No.2 in respect of said car and its validity as on the date of accident, are not in dispute.

Further, the above oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner has remained undisputed by the respondent No.1, who is the owner of car bearing Reg.
No.KA-13-N-5358, as he did not choose to file written statement and contest the case of the petitioner.

Whereas, the respondent No.2 insurance company has denied the above averred facts and circumstances of the accident and taken specific defence that, the accident has occurred solely due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of the motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-13-EM-2481 and dashing the same to car bearing Reg. No.KA-13-N-5358 and there was no negligence on the part of the driver of said car.
The respondent No.2 has not adduced any evidence to establish the said contentions.

But, the documents produced and got marked by the petitioner as Ex.P.1 to 6 itself Anu K.A vs Shivaraj T.E on 6 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/104718617/
4 clearly establishes that, the accident in question has taken place due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of the motorcycle bearing No.KA-13-EM-2481, on the wrong side of the road and dashing the same to oncoming car bearing Reg. No.KA-13-N-5358 of the respondent No.1 and there was no fault on the part of the driver of car bearing Reg. No.KA-13-N-5358.
Further it reveals that, in the said accident the petitioner who was pillion rider of the said motorcycle has sustained grievous injuries on her right leg.

13. Further, the Ex.P.3 spot mahazar also clearly speaks that, the said accident has taken place on the left side of 24 feet wide on Tiptur-Bengaluru NH-206 road, near Bommanahalli Gae, Kasaba Hobli, Tiptur Taluk, Tumakuru District, in between the motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-13- EM-2481 and car bearing Reg. No.KA-13-N-5358.
Further, as per the Motor Vehicle Accident Report, which is marked as Ex.P.4, the accident has not taken place due to any mechanical defects in the vehicle involved in the accident.

When the accident was not caused due to any mechanical defects in the vehicle involved in the accident and there was no negligence on the part of the petitioner, then in the present facts and circumstances of the case, it can be presumed that, the said accident had occurred due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of motorcycle bearing Reg.
No.KA-13-EM-2481.

Further, the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner clearly establishes that, the accident in question has taken place due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of the motorcycle proceeding on the wrong side of the road and dashing the same to the oncoming car bearing Reg. No.KA- 13-N-5358 of the respondent No.1.
Further it reveals that, due to the impact, the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries all over the body.

The investigation officer in his Ex.P.6 final report/charge-sheet, has clearly stated that, the said accident is caused due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of the motorcycle and dashing the same to car bearing Reg.
No.KA-13-N-5358 of the respondent No.1.
Admittedly, the Ex.P.6 final report/charge-sheet has not been challenged by the owner or drivers of both the vehicles involved in the accident.

In such circumstances, there is no impediment to believe the final report of the investigation officer and other police records, regarding the date, time and place of accident, involvement of car bearing Reg.
No.KA-13-N-5358 in the said accident, the injuries sustained by the petitioner in the said accident.
Further, the involvement of car bearing Reg. No.KA-13-N-5358 in the accident in question is not disputed by the respondents.
14. Further, on meticulously going through the Ex.P.5 wound certificate it clearly reveals that, the petitioner has suffered grievous injuries in the road traffic accident.
The petitioner has sustained fracture of medial malleolus of right tibia bone.
On the other hand, there is no contrary or rebuttal evidence on record to disbelieve the contents of said medical records of the petitioner.

Therefore, in such circumstances and in the light of above observations, it can safely be held that, the respondents have failed to rebut the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner regarding involvement of insured car bearing Reg. No.KA-13-N-5358 in the accident in question and injuries caused to the petitioner in the said accident.

15. In the instant case, the petitioner is seeking compensation under Section 163-A of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, for the grievous injuries sustained in the road traffic accident, arose out of the usage of car bearing Reg. No.KA- 13-N-5358 on the public road.

It is settled proposition of law that,
under Sec.163-A of Motor Vehicles Act, the claimant need not require to establish that, the injury is Anu K.A vs Shivaraj T.E on 6 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/104718617/
5 caused due to any wrongful act or negligence or default on the part of the driver of the vehicle involved in the accident or of the concerned or of any other person.
But he has to prove the involvement of said vehicle in the alleged accident, resulting in the injury or death of a person.
The liability under Sec.163-A of Motor Vehicles, 1988, is on the principle of no fault.

The petitioner need not require to establish that, the death or permanent disability has arose due to any wrongful act or negligence or default on the part of the driver of the vehicle involved in the accident or of the concerned or of any other person.

The Sec.163-A of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, reads as follows:
163-A. Special Provisions as to payment of compensation on structural formula basis -
(1) Notwithstanding anything contained in this Act or in any other law for the time being in force or instrument having the force of law, the owner of the motor vehicle or the authorised insurer shall be liable to pay in the case of death or permanent disability due to accident arising out of the use of motor vehicle, compensation, as indicated in the Second Schedule, to the legal heirs or the victim, as the case may be.
Explanation - For the purpose of this sub- section, "permanent disability" shall have the same meaning and extent as in the Workmen's Compensations Act, 1923.
2) In any claim for compensation under sub-section (1), the claimant shall not be required to plead or establish that the death or permanent disability in respect of which the claim has been made was due to any wrongful act or neglect or default of the owner of the vehicle or vehicles concerned or of any other person.
3) The Central Government may, keeping in view the cost of living by notification in the Official Gazette, from time to time amend the Second Schedule.
16.

Therefore, in view of above provision of law and for the above stated reasons, this Court is of the considered opinion that, the petitioner has successfully proved that, she has sustained grievous injuries in a road traffic accident taken place on 13-11-2021 at about 8.30 p.m., on B.H. Road NH-206, near Bommenahalli Village Gate, Tiptur Taluk, Tumakuru District, arose out of the usage of car bearing registration No.KA-13-N-5358 of the respondent No.1.
Hence, I answer Issue No.1 in Affirmative.
17. Issue No.2:

While answering the above issue this Court has come to conclusion that, the petitioner has successfully proved that, she has sustained grievous injuries in the accident arose out of the usage of car bearing registration No.KA-13-N-5358.
The medical records placed on record clearly speaks that, the petitioner has sustained fracture of medial malleolus of right tibia bone.

But,
as per the provision of Sec.163-A of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, the owner of the vehicle or the authorised insurer of the said vehicle shall be liable to pay compensation to the victim for permanent disability or to the legal heirs of deceased victim in the case of death, caused in the Anu K.A vs Shivaraj T.E on 6 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/104718617/
6 accident arising out of the use of such motor vehicle, as indicated in the Second Schedule.

The plain reading of the said provision itself makes it clear that, only under two circumstances i.e. in case of death or permanent disability, the owner or the authorised insurer of the vehicle involved in the accident are liable to pay compensation to the victim or legal heirs of deceased victim, as the case may be.
As per the Second Schedule, the compensation payable in case of death shall of Rs.5,00,000/- and in case of permanent disability it shall be Rs.2,50,000/-.
Further, from 01-01-2019, the said compensation amount shall stand increased by 5% annually.
18. In the present case, no doubt as per the medical records placed on record by the petitioner, she has sustained grievous injury i.e. fracture of medial malleolus of right tibia bone.
But, the petitioner has neither adduced any evidence, nor she has produced any document to show that, due to above injury she has suffered permanent disability.
In such circumstances, she is not entitled for any compensation under Section 163-A of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988.

19. But, the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of New India Assurance Company Ltd. V/s Urmila Haidar, reported in 2025 ACJ 244, has clearly held that, "Sec.164 must be given retrospective effect to award the compensation to the accident which has occurred prior to the amendment also."

sentences.text:
The same was followed by the Coordinate Bench of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in MFA No.9652/2013 clubbed with MFA No.9653/2023, dated 02-04-2025.
20.
As per Sec.164 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, there is no need to prove that, the victim has suffered permanent disability.

If it is proved that, the victim has suffered grievous hurt in the accident arising out of the use of motor vehicle, the owner or the authorized insurer of such vehicle is liable to pay compensation of Rs.2,50,000/- to the victim.

The Sec.164 of Motor Vehicles Act,
1988, reads as follows:
164. Payment of compensation in case of death or grievous hurt, etc. - (1)
Notwithstanding anything contained in this Act or in any other law for the time being in force or instrument having the force of law, the owner of the motor vehicle or the authorised insurer shall be liable to pay in the case of death or grievous hurt due to any accident arising out of the use of motor vehicle, a compensation, of a sum of five lakh rupees in case of death or of two and a half lakh rupees in case of grievous hurt to the legal heirs or the victim, as the case may be.
(2) In any claim for compensation under sub- section (1), the claimant shall not be required to plead or establish that the death or grievous hurt in respect of which the claim has been made was due to any wrongful act or neglect or default of the owner of the vehicle or of the vehicle concerned or of any other person.

( 3 ) Where, in respect of death or grievous hurt due to an accident arising out of the use of motor vehicle, compensation has been paid under any other law for the time being in force, such amount of compensation shall be reduced from the amount of compensation payable under this section.

7 21.
In the instant case, the Ex.P.5 wound certificate clearly speaks that, the petitioner has suffered grievous hurt in the accident in question.
As per Ex.P.5 the petitioner has sustained fracture of medial malleolus of right tibia bone.
Therefore, in such circumstances and for the above stated reasons, this Court is of the considered opinion that, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.2,50,000/- from the respondents.

22. In so far as awarding of interest on the compensation is concerned in, MFA No. 103557/16 between Sri Ram General Ins. Co. Ltd., V/s. Smt. Lakshmi and Others (D.D. 20.3.2018), the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka on detailed discussions has fixed the rate of interest @ 6% p.a., holding that as per Sec.34 of C.P.C., the rate of interest that can be awarded on judgments cannot be more than 6% p.a.

sentences.text: Since, Section 149 of Motor Vehicles Act provides for interest on judgments, the interest to be awarded in claim petitions has to be 6% p.a. and not more than that.
Hence, in the present case, interest @ 6% per annum on the compensation amount, is awarded.
23. Liability:
Admittedly, as on the date of accident, the respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.2 is the insurer of the Maruthi Car bearing Reg. No. KA-13-N-5358.
The insurance policy bearing No.0221003121P103833459, issued by the respondent No.2, in respect of Maruthi Car bearing Reg. No. KA-13-N-5358, was valid and inforce, as on the date of accident.
As such, the respondent No.1 being the owner of vehicle involved in the accident is liable to compensate the petitioner for the damage caused to him in the accident arose out of usage of his vehicle.
The respondent No.2 being the insurer of the said vehicle has to indemnify the respondent No.1.
Therefore, the respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
However, the primary liability is on the respondent No.2 insurance company to pay the above compensation to the petitioner.

Therefore, for the above stated reasons, holding that, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.2,50,000/- from the respondent No.2, with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realization, I answer Issue No.2 in Partly Affirmative.
24. Issue No.3:

In view of the above findings, I proceed to pass the following order:
ORDER
The petition is partly allowed with costs.
The petitioner is entitled to compensation of Rs.2,50,000/- (Rupees two lakh fifty thousand only), with interest at the rate of 6% per annum, from the date of petition till its realization.
The respondent No.1 & 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the above compensation amount to the petitioner.

However, the primary liability to pay the compensation amount is fastened on respondent No.2 - Insurance Company and it is directed to pay the compensation amount within two months from the date of this order.

The entire compensation amount with proportionate interest shall be released in favour of the petitioner through e-payment on proper identification and verification.
Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.2,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
